headline: High prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Cline’s workspace/browser outputs can flow into Semantic Kernel plugins and shared memory without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline ingests browser content and workspace files, and Semantic Kernel can consume MCP/OpenAPI/plugin inputs. With Cline’s shared filesystem state and SK’s plugin-driven function calling, attacker-controlled content from A can be treated as instructions by B. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation, so the interaction is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Cline reads untrusted web content into workspace files and Semantic Kernel parses that content as plugin input, injection is plausible.
IF the pair shares a filesystem or memory store without provenance tags, attacker instructions can cross from A to B.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A→B payloads before B parses them.
Restrict B to allowlisted plugin schemas for one test run.
Disable automatic ingestion of browser-sourced text into B.
Use separate workspaces or directories for A and B.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and provenance enforcement at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots, while Semantic Kernel touches application context and can send data to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face or MCP servers. Because both read/write files and share state via filesystem or memory store, sensitive workspace data can leak from A into B’s outputs or upstream APIs in default setups.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace or memory store, files from A can be surfaced to B.
IF B is configured with a third-party model provider, application context may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces.
Remove secrets from shared files before B runs.
Point B to a local-only model for a quick test.
Limit B’s memory store to non-sensitive summaries.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on shared state.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem and modify git state; Semantic Kernel can also write files and use MCP-backed tools. Their shared-state mechanisms differ, but both can mutate the same workspace or application-defined files, creating overlapping writes and race conditions. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF A modifies git state while B writes generated artifacts, repository state can diverge without locks.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Pause one agent while the other commits changes.
Use git worktrees for parallel runs.
Turn off B writes for a short validation pass.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce code, browser-derived facts, and file edits; Semantic Kernel is a kernel+plugins agent pattern that can treat upstream outputs as function inputs. If B consumes A’s outputs without verification, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into downstream actions or generated artifacts. The profiles show no built-in verification step between them.
conditions: IF B uses A’s generated text as authoritative plugin input, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF A’s browser-derived content is rendered or acted on by B without checks, downstream mistakes can become operational.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require B to re-derive critical facts from primary sources.
Block direct execution of A-generated commands.
Log A→B transformations for spot checks.
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source-of-truth data.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots, while Semantic Kernel handles application context and may route it to third-party model providers or MCP servers. If regulated or sensitive data is present, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches because A and B have different storage and API paths. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Cline’s workspace and then forwarded through Semantic Kernel to a third-party provider, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention policies differ between the workspace and the memory store, deletion/export handling can diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Use a local-only provider for B.
Delete temporary artifacts after each session.
Document retention for both tools before deployment.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and DPA controls across the pair.
